title: PRESSER | Pete Golding - Wofford Preview (11-17-26)
text: Guess P, I think it reports kind of came out maybe Friday or or so about K-Wan being out for the year. Just wanted to get confirmation or your comments on that. >> Yeah, I mean definitely obviously I was working with Pat and trying to figure through the rehab process and all that and it was just to a point that it wasn't getting better and it was looking like it was going to be long term, so made the decision to go ahead and fix it. So he got a fix last week in Dallas. Had to follow up today, so should be back tomorrow. >> You you're on your fourth running back a little bit. I know you're high on on Josh Die kind of in the off season bringing him in. I just wanted your your read on on how he played against OU and kind of you know where where that room's at right now. >> Yeah, I thought you know start with Shaka. I thought Shaka played really well you know early and then he you know bumped up the ankle a little bit and got x-rayed at halftime. I thought Josh came in there, gave us a little bit of a spark. You know I think he probably wants one play back you know the the one drop out of the backfield, but it's a guy that's consistently done it right, you know and a guy that we know we could count on to do things right both in the protection and in the run game. So I think it was good for him to get in and I thought he came in and responded. It didn't feel different didn't look different, you know. I think you know when you actually look at the stats I mean we rushed for our play more than they did, you know when you look at the game and you wouldn't have thought that coming out of it, but but that's what it was, but I was impressed with Shaka's toughness. I think he's a different back that we've seen this year and the ability to fall forward, but I was proud of Josh how he got in there and competed both in the run game and the protection. They got a bunch of different looks, a lot of seven up stuff and then the ability to catch the ball in the backfield needs to be a little more consistent, but he had a couple of those as well. >> And how are Shaka and Makai doing in terms of injury or potentially playing that next week or later this season? >> we're still evaluating the Shaka situation. It's it's being a high ankle, so you know we'll kind of probably be week to week with that be honest with you. I think that's a game time decision at best probably for this week to be honest with you. You know the Makai piece was a thumb week that was a concern from a protection standpoint and all those. So hopefully that should be an issue, you know, this week at all and I would expect him to be available. >> What has the response been from the team in the 24 48 hours, whatever it's been since you guys got back? >> Yeah I mean obviously walking off the field, you know, kind of talked about the the disappointment component of it of walking off the field and all that and we just to be honest with you it kind of hit him right in the face after the game. I mean this this is life man. Like it doesn't always go as planned. Uh you're going to have adversity um and when you get punched in the face, how are you going to respond? Um you know I think today we gave them off yesterday, you know, getting back and we brought them in this morning and really evaluated the tape of the things that we got to correct and clean up and all that. But you know this to me is strictly going to be based on the character and the competitive character of who we really are. And and that was my challenge to them. It's this is going to happen a lot in your life man and it's not going to go exactly like you think and you get punched in the face, whether that's your marriage, whether that's being a parent, whether that's your job. Um and I think the mistake that a lot of us make is you know you always say that fork in the road. Like to me there's never a fork. Like you know you don't have the option of going two directions. Like there's one road, and it's hard, and it's not easy. Um, but it takes mental toughness, and you know, I think that's the one thing this group that we've talked about throughout, you know, the year consistently like the choices and decisions that we make, that they don't only affect me; they affect everybody in this room. And I think, when you look at some of the games that haven't ended the way that we want to, whether it's offense, defense, or special teams, a lot of the things that come up it's one of the 11 guys, you know, that that had made a choice to not do it the right way, or, you know, from a coaching perspective, of not having them in the right place. But you know I think that [snorts] was the biggest thing, my selling point to them is like this is a life lesson right now. It's not always going to go the way that we want it to and you got to really look back and really evaluate and really look in the mirror. Did we do everything that we potentially could control prior to it to give us ourselves our best shot. And you know, I think for some of these weeks we didn't. And I think that's been the frustrating part, you know, for all of us. There there's been times that it's looked exactly how it's supposed to and this is what it should be and here's the result and then the consistency in that. But I think a lot of that's based on the decision making and the choices that we all make, you know, Monday through Friday. >> Pete, there's eight teams this morning, you know, that are within a game, three or four losses, four at the top then and four at the bottom. Are you surprised at this or is this the new norm now in the SEC? >> Yeah, I mean, I would say the surprise... I know, you know, there's no surprise to me in this league after I've been in it 10 years. You know, you got to show up weekend and week out, and you know, there's so much, you know, more to it as far as, you know, who's available, who's healthy, where's the game being played. I mean, there's a lot that goes into this league. I think when the talent starts getting close, you know, I I think the difference in this league's always been one possession games. You you know, and I think to win this league and be successful and make the playoffs, you got to find a way to win one possession games. And I think it's no different when you look at the 24 season compared to the 23 season. You know, all those 10 win seasons regardless where you're at in the SEC that you're going to go back and look at those one possession games is somehow you found a way to make a play to win the game. And we've not been able to do that, you know, this year when you think about the Texas, when you think about this one. You know, I think the difference right now is kind of the starting of games. You know, you look up to Texas is 24 3. You look up in this one is 14 nothing. You know, you never felt like at least I never felt like defensively like, oh man, here we go. Like it was never that feeling. Felt like we had control of the game. Messed up a couple third downs and give them a touchdown early. And then the punt return hits and then you look up, it's 14 0, you know, and the weather and all that type of stuff and and you make it really hard for yourself. And you never expect them to play perfect. You're not going to play perfect, but you know, some some of those mistakes that we've made in those games have been catastrophic uh felt like you could never get momentum. And to be honest with you, you know, a lot of those years in my opinion that you've made the runs and all that, you know, there's sometimes there's a call here, the ball bounce here, you know, that you can still do things right and not have the success that you want as well, you know. So I think sometimes the ball's got to bounce your way a little bit, uh which hasn't felt that way, you know, this year for some reason, but we haven't helped ourselves with it. But I think there is a lot of parity now based on the structure of the portal and everything else to your point, uh very much more NFL model. Um, and you know, there's very rarely that any of those guys are undefeated, you know, much less a season, much less right now. I mean, you look at all those rosters. So uh you got to find a way from a coaching perspective to get them up every week and have really good plans and be able to hold them accountable and develop [snorts] the right habits throughout the week. And so I think the guys that are doing that better on a consistent basis are giving themselves the best chance. >> Pete, I know you're not looking for excuses, but uh how difficult was all the changing plans and the travel problems and all that junk? >> Yeah, I think that kind of goes back into the mental toughness component of things. And I think it kind of goes back into the mindset kind of that we've been looking for all year that I think you have to have to play championship football is like put your energy and focus on the things that you can control. And I think so many times, you know, we focus on the outside noise and other things that we really have no control over. And then now our focus is off of what's important and it's the focus and attention to detail to me to do my job for you know, on a consistent basis. So you know, I don't think, you know, that had a lot to do with it because I felt like on Saturday when they came back in, I also almost felt like there was a different energy kind of like I said after the game. Like it broke up the monotony of the week. It was a little bit different, you know, felt very COVID. I thought there was a little new energy within the team. So I don't think that had as much to do with I think when you look at this point in the year of, you know, how have you managed the roster from an injury standpoint? And when you look at going on the road in the SEC and you got $8 million on the out list, you know what I'm saying? I mean, some other guys got to be able to step up and take advantage of those opportunities. And I think we had some guys that did. Um and then I think we had some guys that that didn't. So I don't think it was much of the travel component and all of that as it was, you know, the execution piece. Um and then I think there's a, you know, no different than the NFL. When you invest in certain guys at certain positions and they're not available, it's different, right? You you want to have guys behind them and have them ready to roll and they got to step up and all that. But there's a reason why guys make a different different amount of money, you know, and all those type of things. Um but I think everybody's going through that this year. And you know, I've seen the stat of the injuries this year. I know it's been talked about, you know, a bunch and all that. But uh I I I don't put anything on it on the traveling component of it to be honest with you. [snorts] >> Pete, all all all season it seems like Bryson Sanders has gone down. You've gone out and checked on him. It looks like he comes off the field and yet he keeps coming back. What does that say about him as a as a player and also maybe more importantly as a person? >> Yeah, I mean, I I I think, you know, that's what I mentioned to this group this morning. There's a lot in this group that are like that, that that are Brysons of the world and the Cooteses of the world that are tough, competitive. They love football and they'll do anything for their teammates. And and he's a guy that a lot of people probably wouldn't have been right out there the first snap based on what he had and how banged up that thing was and what it's looked like the last couple of weeks. But you know, he he he's a guy to me that his investment is different than a lot of these other guys. He came here right out of high school. You know, we got senior week coming up this week, right? It it's senior game and you know, I I was looking at the stat, you know, they're 40 and 11 right now, that group. You know, and they have the opportunity to go win three more. They'll be the winningest class in the history of the program. This place means something to him and he's put a lot into this. And so, you know, I think he knew, you know, what was on the line to go out there and compete for his teammates and compete for Ole Miss and the fans and the alumni to give ourselves an opportunity to continue to compete for a championship. So uh dude's a warrior, man. Um he's wired the right way. He loves this place. He loves the game and he's going to give everything he's got regardless if he's 100% or not. And we need more like him. >> Uh Tareeq Dunson, I know he was playing a hand injury and Kutas obviously out. Do you have any update on those guys and I guess the rest of the season for them? >> Yeah, so obviously I think Kutas Kutas was definitely still be out this week. You know, Sherif had a broken thumb and so last week he had a decision to make. Could he could he get it fixed last week and sit out the game or get it fixed after the game and play the game and he chose to play for his team which I really appreciate and he played his butt off and it wasn't perfect, but he played a heck of a game. So he's had surgery since then. So we got the thumb fixed. So he'll probably be out this week as well. >> And maybe a cheesy question, but you talked about senior day and things like that. Just what does this class mean to you? I know guys like I mean Nick Cole or Jahiem Otis that you've had prior relationships with and things like that. [snorts] >> I I think a lot of them too, man. Like cuz coming over here in '23, you know, I've been with you know, the guys that had came in here out of high school like through this run. Haven't had the same relationship that I have with them now prior to, especially, they're on the other side of the ball. And then there's so many other previous relationships of guys now with the portal that you bring in and all those type of things. And you know, I I think one of the things about this place to me, and that's what I was telling the guys this morning, like, you know, there's a real piece to an elite program and I've told y'all this before that it's not always about when you got your cleats on. You know, elite programs in my opinion are designed for when you take your cleats off and I think that's what's so special about this place and the people and I think this day is no different for that. I mean, I think the culmination for the fans and their appreciation of what it's been like for them to play in the Vault in front of unbelievable crowds, and what the people, you know, in this town, this community, and obviously the school have done for them and I think there's going to be a real appreciation from the fans for what this group's done for them and to be able to go out of here the winningest class, you know, in the history of the program. I think senior day's a little different now than it used to be. All those used to be fourth and fifth year guys or some of them now, you know, have potentially done it somewhere else too. And so but for those ones that came out of high school and and did it the right way and and stayed committed and all that, man, I think it's a sign of resiliency, especially in today's age. I think it's an understanding of what this place can do for them for the next 40 to 50 years, which I think is awesome to see. So, just really happy for them to be able to experience it. >> Coach, what about Cam [clears throat] and Keaton and Edwin Joseph and Ky Frazier? Any update on those guys? >> Yeah, you know, Edwin obviously still week to week. You know, based on he did ground running last week. And so we'll monitor [clears throat] that throughout the week. Obviously if he'll be able to go, you know, we'll get him back out there in a game environment. It's been a long time since he's played, so that isn't one that we'll wait on if he's cleared to go. You know, Keaton's going to be down for a while, you know, with the knee and the ankle on that and going in and getting that thing fixed like he did. So I don't foresee him You know, I think that [clears throat] one probably would be bowl game at best to Keaton Thomas. I I think that one would be the bowl game depending upon when it is. Probably at best just, you know, playing these three within a 14-day window based on what they have is really tough. So I think, you know, those guys will be bowl game. [snorts] And who's the other one you asked? >> Cam Frank. >> Cam we'll monitor Cam. We'll shut down this week for sure and try to get him back for for the Egg Bowl, which I I assume that he'll be available. >> Pete, you've talked a couple of times about the NFL model and how college is looking more like the NFL than ever. One of the things the NFL does a lot is they'll take a look at what they have coming next season. Is that something you see yourself doing these last couple of weeks? >> You know, I I think the difference in the model between the NFL and the college to me is the responsibility of the head coach in my opinion, right? And I think it's number one to put the best guys out there to win the football game number one. Like I've got a job to do, right? And we've got to finish this thing the right way. I think that's a mentality regardless who you play or where you play. I think guys that are doing things right on and off the field um that obviously you need to see more of. I think that's what the purpose of these games are, right? And no disrespect to Wofford. I mean, they're a good football team and all that, but um there's a reason those guys went there and the reason the guys went here. So, you know, hopefully this is an opportunity for some of those other guys to get in game experience to really get a good feel of where they're at um and where's their development and all those type of things um moving forward. And then now a lot of the injuries have created opportunity for a lot of those guys anyway, you know? And so I think you look up even, you know, in in that first first quarter of Oklahoma, you got three true freshmen out there. You you got Curtis playing three technique. You got Landon Barnes playing five technique. You got Dorean Barney at corner, right? So I mean, you already got three true freshmen in in a play in game. Um so this isn't like for a 1AA team. So I think a lot of the, you know, the injuries and kind of where you're at, some of those freshmen that got unique ability have been playing anyway. But I think definitely this is an opportunity for some of those younger guys, uh, to have an opportunity to go in and show what they can do with their opportunity, and I think it's important for them to play well. >> Holistically, what what's been your assessment of Deuce Alexander season? >> Yeah, so I think up and down. Um you know, I think uh he's been banged up a little bit, you know. I think um I think he's one of the most explosive players we have, you know? And I said, you know, his comparison to me has always been J-Mo. And I think his A to B uh I think he's elite. Got elite top end speed. I think he presents a lot of problems for defenses. Um I think when you become that type of player and he had early success, um games become harder for you because they got plans for you, you know? And I think that's why it's really really important especially that position to have multiple guys that present problems. Um you know, and you got to be able to run the football as well, you know, to change pitchers and do different things to create some one-on-ones you want. Um but I think, you know, the consistency of you know, catching the football on a consistent basis, you know, sometimes hasn't always been what it should be and he'll be the first one to tell you that, but you know, I love Deuce. I think he's one of the most explosive players that we have. He's got an extremely bright future. Um, he's a vertical threat for us and I think a big piece, you know, moving forward. He's going to have a lot of opportunity. Um, you know, I think, you know, play well these next couple games and then he's got to really evaluate, all right, what's this NFL thing look like and where where are my draftable grades at and what's realistic and what's not. But um, I think he's super explosive. Think he'll become more consistent and he knows that, but a really good player for us. >> Yep. Sorry, it was tough. >> Coach, in a game like this where, you know, you maybe feel a little bit of a favorite in this game, is there an idea to maybe looking towards the future and playing a guy like Deuce Knight maybe a little bit more than normal, you know, than trying to dab? >> Yeah, it's it's it's to me, you know, I've been in several of these in this league. You, you're still going to the game with the right preparation and the right mindset, like this is an SEC game to start the game. And then, hopefully, you challenge your guys that we've got a mindset regarding, you know, around here to spot the ball regardless who we play or where we play, to come out there and make it look like what it's supposed to. And then hopefully if you do that and get it into a position to where you're in control, uh then you create a lot of opportunity for other guys to really get, you know, in-game film of them in certain situations. And I think it's really important now that, you know, that that this model now has gone to, you know, a lot of coaches take a lot of flak in postgame after some of these games based on the flow of the game and why are you still throwing it? Why are you still doing that? Like there's a real piece now, hey, you got to know what you have, right? And the ability to retain and all those type of things. On the other piece of it, a lot of these guys work their butt off all year and they're, you know, they have the right to give them the opportunity to go in there and compete and run the offense and play defense and all that. So uh yeah, hopefully it gets to a point to where those guys that can play winning football in this league have the opportunity to go into a game and show that and display that for them and for us. And I think that's a really important piece to get it to that point. >> All right, thanks guys. >> Appreciate it, fellas. [snorts]
